election._note: D'Hondt in six constituencies with nine levelling seats, reduced to national PR with the 5% national gate that decides who shares the levelling seats. The snap election of 30 November 2024 opened a four-year term, so the next is due by November 2028. Constitution of Iceland, Art. 31; Wikipedia, '2024 Icelandic parliamentary election'.

dissolution._note: The President dissolves the Althing on the Prime Minister's advice (Art. 24), which is how the 2024 snap election was called -- MLT's executive-advice shape, which the parliamentary_republic template reads as self_dissolution, the gap recorded here. Polling within 45 days. Constitution of Iceland, Art. 24.

head_of_state._note: The President, directly elected for four years with no term limit; elected 1 June 2024 and inaugurated 1 August, so the next falls in June 2028. Largely ceremonial, with the Art. 26 power to refer a bill to referendum by declining to sign it -- unmodelled. Constitution of Iceland, Arts. 5-6, 26.
head_of_state.title: President

amendment._note: Art. 79: an amendment passed by the Althing triggers a dissolution and an election, and the new Althing must pass it unchanged -- a SIMPLE majority twice with an election between. The template carries two_thirds only; the machinery reads the intervening election's cost as that bar, the honest difference recorded here. Constitution of Iceland, Art. 79.
amendment._referendum_note: Only the church provision (Art. 79, second paragraph) requires a referendum; the rest of the constitution amends without one. Constitution of Iceland, Art. 79.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: No eternity clause; the 1944 republican constitution has been revised by the Art. 79 procedure several times.

judicial._note: The ordinary courts, led by the Supreme Court (Haestirettur), review whether an Act conflicts with the constitution in the case before them -- decentralised review on the Nordic pattern. Constitution of Iceland, Art. 2; Supreme Court practice since 1943.

formation._note: The President gives a party leader the mandate to form a government; there is no investiture vote and a coalition governs until a no-confidence motion carries by simple majority. Coalition negotiation is the plain reading -- the 2024 government is a three-party coalition. Constitution of Iceland, Arts. 15, 24.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Iceland's crown was the Danish king's until 1944; the restored line is the house's invention, as MLT's is.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD/Statistics Iceland ~2024, rounded, on SWE.json's conventions. VAT 24% standard; corporate 20%; income 34 is the FITTED EFFECTIVE rate on AUT's and IRL's convention -- the statutory 31.5-46.3% brackets at their middle would model 35.3% of GDP against the 34% collected, and the model's revenue must not exceed the nation's; capital gains 22% on capital income; no wealth tax since 2015. Revenue ~34% of GDP is the OECD Revenue Statistics figure. Gross debt ~61% of GDP. Defence 0.1% because Iceland keeps no armed forces -- the coast guard and NATO host costs are the line. Pensions 3.0% is low because the occupational funds are funded and sit outside the state. Spending scaled to expenditure near 43% of GDP.
